questions.q:
With reference to investments, consider the following:
I. Bonds
II. Hedge Funds
III. Stocks
IV. Venture Capital
How many of the above are treated as Alternative Investment Funds?
questions.e: Hedge funds and venture capital funds are privately pooled funds registered with SEBI as Alternative Investment Funds. Bonds and stocks are securities, not AIFs.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q1

questions.q:
Which of the following are the sources of income for the Reserve Bank of India?
I. Buying and selling Government bonds
II. Buying and selling foreign currency
III. Pension fund management
IV. Lending to private companies
V. Printing and distributing currency notes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The RBI earns from its holdings and trading of government bonds and foreign currency assets. Printing notes is an expense, and it neither manages pension funds nor lends to private companies.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q2

questions.q:
With reference to the Government of India, consider the following information: Organization Some of its functions It works under
I. Directorate of Enforcement Enforcement of the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 Internal Security Division–I, Ministry of Home Affairs
II. Directorate of Revenue Intelligence Enforces the Provisions of the Customs Act, 1962 Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
III. Directorate General of Systems and Data Management Carrying out big data analytics to assist tax officers for better policy and nabbing tax evaders Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance In how many of the above rows is the information correctly matched?
questions.e: The DRI enforces the Customs Act under the Department of Revenue. The ED is under the Department of Revenue, not the Home Ministry, and big data analytics for tax officers is done by a different directorate.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q3

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Reserve Bank of India mandates all the listed companies in India to submit a Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR).
II. In India, a company submitting a BRSR makes disclosures in the report that are largely non-financial in nature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The BRSR is a SEBI requirement for the top 1,000 listed companies, not an RBI rule for all. Its disclosures are mostly non-financial ESG information.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In India, income from allied agricultural activities like poultry farming and wool rearing in rural areas is exempted from any tax.
Statement-II: In India, rural agricultural land is not considered a capital asset under the provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Only agricultural income from land is exempt; poultry or wool income is taxable. Rural agricultural land is excluded from 'capital asset' under Section 2(14).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India has joined the Minerals Security Partnership as a member.
II. India is a resource-rich country in all the 30 critical minerals that it has identified.
III. The Parliament in 2023 has amended the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 empowering the Central Government to exclusively auction mining lease and composite license for certain critical minerals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India joined the Minerals Security Partnership in 2023, and the 2023 MMDR amendment lets the Centre auction certain critical minerals. India is import-dependent for many critical minerals, so II is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q6

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: As regards returns from an investment in a company, generally, bondholders are considered to be relatively at lower risk than stockholders.
Statement-II: Bondholders are lenders to a company whereas stockholders are its owners.
Statement-III: For repayment purpose, bondholders are prioritized over stockholders by a company.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement I explains Statement II
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: Bondholders are lenders and are repaid before stockholders, who are owners. Both reasons explain why bonds carry lower risk.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q7

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India accounts for a very large portion of all equity option contracts traded globally thus exhibiting a great boom.
II. India's stock market has grown rapidly in the recent past even overtaking Hong Kong's at some point of time.
III. There is no regulatory body either to warn the small investors about the risks of options trading or to act on unregistered financial advisors in this regard.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India leads the world in equity options contracts and its market briefly overtook Hong Kong's. SEBI regulates and warns about options trading and acts against unregistered advisers, so III is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q8

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Circular economy reduces the emissions of greenhouse gases.
Statement-II: Circular economy reduces the use of raw materials as inputs.
Statement-III: Circular economy reduces wastage in the production process.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: A circular economy uses fewer raw materials and cuts waste, and both reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Both explain Statement-I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q9

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Capital receipts create a liability or cause a reduction in the assets of the Government.
II. Borrowings and disinvestment are capital receipts.
III. Interest received on loans creates a liability of the Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Capital receipts create liabilities or reduce assets; borrowing and disinvestment are examples. Interest received is revenue and creates no liability.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q10

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Raja Ram Mohan Roy:
I. He possessed great love and respect for the traditional philosophical systems of the East.
II. He desired his countrymen to accept the rational and scientific approach and the principle of human dignity and social equality of all men and women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Rammohun Roy respected the Vedanta and Upanishads while urging reason, science, human dignity and equality for women. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q11

questions.q:
Consider the following subjects with regard to Non-Cooperation Programme:
I. Boycott of law-courts and foreign cloth
II. Observance of strict non-violence
III. Retention of titles and honours without using them in public
IV. Establishment of Panchayats for settling disputes
How many of the above were parts of Non-Cooperation Programme?
questions.e: The programme included boycotting courts and foreign cloth, strict non-violence and setting up panchayats. Titles were to be surrendered, not kept.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q12

questions.q: The irrigation device called 'Araghatta' was
o: a water bag made of leather pulled over a pulley
a large wheel with earthen pots tied to the outer ends of its spokes
a larger earthen pot driven by bullocks
a large water bucket pulled up by rope directly by hand
questions.e: The araghatta was a wheel with pots tied around it that lifted water from a well as it turned.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q13

questions.q: Who among the following rulers in ancient India had assumed the titles 'Mattavilasa', 'Vichitrachitta' and 'Gunabhara'?
questions.e: The Pallava king Mahendravarman I took titles such as Mattavilasa, Vichitrachitta and Gunabhara; he also wrote the play Mattavilasa Prahasana.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q14

questions.q: Fa-hien (Faxian), the Chinese pilgrim, travelled to India during the reign of
questions.e: Faxian visited India around 399-414 CE, during the reign of Chandragupta II.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q15

questions.q: Who among the following led a successful military campaign against the kingdom of Srivijaya, the powerful maritime State, which ruled the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java and the neighbouring islands?
questions.e: Rajendra I Chola sent a naval expedition that defeated Srivijaya in the 1020s.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q16

questions.q:
With reference to ancient India (600–322 BC), consider the following pairs: Territorial region River flowing in the region
I. Asmaka Godavari
II. Kamboja Vipas
III. Avanti Mahanadi
IV. Kosala Sarayu
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Asmaka was on the Godavari and Kosala on the Sarayu. Kamboja was in the north-west and Avanti in Malwa, not on the Beas or Mahanadi.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q17

questions.q: The first Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, a music training school, was set up in 1901 by Vishnu Digambar Paluskar in
questions.e: Vishnu Digambar Paluskar set up the first Gandharva Mahavidyalaya in Lahore in 1901.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q18

questions.q: Ashokan inscriptions suggest that the 'Pradeshika', 'Rajuka' and 'Yukta' were important officers at the
questions.e: Ashoka's edicts show rajukas, pradeshikas and yuktas as officers running the districts.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q19

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the Non-Cooperation Movement:
I. The Congress declared the attainment of 'Swaraj' by all legitimate and peaceful means to be its objective.
II. It was to be implemented in stages with civil disobedience and non-payment of taxes for the next stage only if 'Swaraj' did not come within a year and the Government resorted to repression.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: At Nagpur (1920) the Congress adopted swaraj by legitimate and peaceful means as its goal, and Non-Cooperation was planned in stages, with civil disobedience to follow. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q20

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
I. Austria
II. Bulgaria
III. Croatia
IV. Serbia
V. Sweden
VI. North Macedonia
How many of the above are members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization?
questions.e: Bulgaria, Croatia, North Macedonia and Sweden are NATO members. Austria and Serbia are not.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q21

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
I. Bolivia
II. Brazil
III. Colombia
IV. Ecuador
V. Paraguay
VI. Venezuela Andes mountains pass through how many of the above countries?
questions.e: The Andes pass through Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela among these. Brazil and Paraguay lie east of them.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q22

questions.q:
Consider the following water bodies:
I. Lake Tanganyika
II. Lake Tonlé Sap
III. Patos Lagoon Through how many of them does the equator pass?
questions.e: The equator passes through none of them: Tanganyika lies south of it, Tonlé Sap is in Cambodia and Patos Lagoon in southern Brazil.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q23

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about turmeric during the year 2022–23:
I. India is the largest producer and exporter of turmeric in the world.
II. More than 30 varieties of turmeric are grown in India.
III. Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are major turmeric producing States in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India is the largest producer and exporter of turmeric, grows over 30 varieties, and Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are major producers. All three, per UPSC's key.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q24

questions.q:
Which of the following are the evidences of the phenomenon of continental drift?
I. The belt of ancient rocks from Brazil coast matches with those from Western Africa.
II. The gold deposits of Ghana are derived from the Brazil plateau when the two continents lay side by side.
III. The Gondwana system of sediments from India is known to have its counterparts in six different landmasses of the Southern Hemisphere.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Matching rock belts in Brazil and West Africa, Ghana's gold traced to Brazilian sources, and Gondwana sediments across southern landmasses all support continental drift.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q25

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The amount of dust particles in the atmosphere is more in subtropical and temperate areas than in equatorial and polar regions.
Statement-II: Subtropical and temperate areas have less dry winds.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Dust is higher over subtropical and temperate belts because they have more dry winds, not fewer. Statement-II is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q26

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In January, in the Northern Hemisphere, the isotherms bend equatorward while crossing the landmasses, and poleward while crossing the oceans.
Statement-II: In January, the air over the oceans is warmer than that over the landmasses in the Northern Hemisphere.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
questions.e: In January oceans are warmer than land in the Northern Hemisphere, so isotherms bend poleward over oceans and equatorward over land. II explains I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q27

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: In the context of effect of water on rocks, chalk is known as a very permeable rock whereas clay is known as quite an impermeable or least permeable rock.
Statement II: Chalk is porous and hence can absorb water.
Statement III: Clay is not at all porous.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: Chalk is porous and permeable, which explains Statement I. Clay is actually very porous but impermeable, so Statement III is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q28

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Without the atmosphere, temperature would be well below freezing point everywhere on the Earth's surface.
II. Heat absorbed and trapped by the atmosphere maintains our planet's average temperature.
III. Atmosphere's gases, like carbon dioxide, are particularly good at absorbing and trapping radiation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Without the atmosphere Earth would be far below freezing; greenhouse gases like CO₂ absorb and trap heat to keep the average near 15°C. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q29

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rashtriya Gokul Mission:
I. It is important for the upliftment of rural poor as majority of low producing indigenous animals are with small and marginal farmers and landless labourers.
II. It was initiated to promote indigenous cattle and buffalo rearing and conservation in a scientific and holistic manner.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Rashtriya Gokul Mission promotes indigenous cattle and buffalo breeds scientifically, and helps the rural poor who own most indigenous animals. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q30

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Studies indicate that carbon dioxide emissions from cement industry account for more than 5% of global carbon emissions.
Statement II: Silica-bearing clay is mixed with limestone while manufacturing cement.
Statement III: Limestone is converted into lime during clinker production for cement manufacturing.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: Cement causes about 7% of global CO₂. Both statements about manufacture are true, but only the conversion of limestone to lime (releasing CO₂) explains it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q31

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: At the 28th United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP28), India refrained from signing the 'Declaration on Climate and Health'.
Statement II: The COP28 Declaration on Climate and Health is a binding declaration; and if signed, it becomes mandatory to decarbonize health sector.
Statement III: If India's health sector is decarbonized, the resilience of its health-care system may be compromised.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: India did not sign the COP28 health declaration. The declaration is non-binding, so II is wrong; India's concern was that decarbonising health care could affect resilience.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q32

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Scientific studies suggest that a shift is taking place in the Earth’s rotation and axis.
Statement II: Solar flares and associated coronal mass ejections bombarded the Earth’s outermost atmosphere with tremendous amount of energy.
Statement III: As the Earth’s polar ice melts, the water tends to move towards the equator.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: Melting polar ice shifts mass towards the equator and alters Earth's rotation and axis. Solar storms are real but do not shift the axis.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q33

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement on climate change is frequently discussed in global discussions on sustainable development and climate change.
Statement II: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement on climate change sets out the principles of carbon markets.
Statement III: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement on climate change intends to promote inter-country non-market strategies to reach their climate targets.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: Article 6 covers both carbon markets and non-market cooperation between countries, which is why it is widely discussed. Both explain Statement I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q34

questions.q: Which one of the following launched the ‘Nature Solutions Finance Hub for Asia and the Pacific’?
o: The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)
questions.e: The Asian Development Bank launched the Nature Solutions Finance Hub for Asia and the Pacific at COP28.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q35

questions.q:
With reference to ‘Direct Air Capture’, an emerging technology, which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. It can be used as a way of carbon sequestration.
II. It can be a valuable approach for plastic production and in food processing.
III. In aviation, it can be a source of carbon for combining with hydrogen to create synthetic low-carbon fuel.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: None of the above statements is correct
questions.e: Direct air capture can store CO₂, supply it for plastics and food processing, and combine it with hydrogen for synthetic aviation fuel. All three.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q36

questions.q:
Regarding Peacock tarantula (Gooty tarantula), consider the following statements:
I. It is an omnivorous crustacean.
II. Its natural habitat in India is only limited to some forest areas.
III. In its natural habitat, it is an arboreal species.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Gooty tarantula is a tree-dwelling spider found only in a few Eastern Ghats forests. It is an arachnid, not a crustacean, and is carnivorous.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q37

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in India are less than 0.5 t CO2/capita.
II. In terms of CO2 emissions from fuel combustion, India ranks second in Asia-Pacific region.
III. Electricity and heat producers are the largest sources of CO2 emissions in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India emits about 2 t CO₂ per person, more than 0.5 t. It is second in Asia-Pacific after China, and power and heat are its largest source.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q38

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Plant Description
I. Cassava Woody shrub
II. Ginger Herb with pseudostem
III. Malabar spinach Herbaceous climber
IV. Mint Annual shrub
V. Papaya Woody shrub
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Cassava is a woody shrub, ginger a herb with a pseudostem and Malabar spinach a climber. Mint is a perennial herb and papaya a tree-like herb.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q39

questions.q:
With reference to the planet Earth, consider the following statements:
I. Rain forests produce more oxygen than that produced by oceans.
II. Marine phytoplankton and photosynthetic bacteria produce about 50% of world’s oxygen.
III. Well-oxygenated surface water contains several folds higher oxygen than that in atmospheric air.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
o: None of the above statements is correct
questions.e: Marine phytoplankton and photosynthetic bacteria produce about half the world's oxygen, more than rainforests. Water holds far less oxygen than air.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q40

questions.q:
Consider the following types of vehicles:
I. Full battery electric vehicles
II. Hydrogen fuel cell vehicles
III. Fuel cell-electric hybrid vehicles
How many of the above are considered as alternative powertrain vehicles?
questions.e: Battery-electric, hydrogen fuel cell and fuel cell-electric hybrid vehicles all count as alternative powertrains.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q41

questions.q:
With reference to Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), consider the following statements:
I. All types of UAVs can do vertical landing.
II. All types of UAVs can do automated hovering.
III. All types of UAVs can use battery only as a source of power supply.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fixed-wing UAVs cannot hover or land vertically, and drones can run on fuel as well as batteries. None of the 'all UAVs' claims holds.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q42

questions.q:
In the context of electric vehicle batteries, consider the following elements:
I. Cobalt
II. Graphite
III. Lithium
IV. Nickel
How many of the above usually make up battery cathodes?
questions.e: EV battery cathodes use lithium with nickel and cobalt (as in NMC). Graphite is the anode.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q43

questions.q:
Consider the following:
I. Cigarette butts
II. Eyeglass lenses
III. Car tyres
How many of them contain plastic?
questions.e: Cigarette filters are cellulose acetate, many spectacle lenses are plastic, and tyres contain synthetic polymers. All three contain plastic.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q44
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following substances:
I. Ethanol
II. Nitroglycerine
III. Urea Coal gasification technology can be used in the production of how many of them?
questions.e: Syngas from coal gasification can make ethanol and ammonia/urea. Nitroglycerine is made by nitrating glycerine.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q45

questions.q: What is the common characteristic of the chemical substances generally known as CL-20, HMX and LLM-105, which are sometimes talked about in media?
o: These are alternatives to hydro-fluorocarbon refrigerants
These are explosives in military weapons
These are high-energy fuels for cruise missiles
These are fuels for rocket propulsion
questions.e: CL-20, HMX and LLM-105 are high explosives used in military munitions.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q46

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. It is expected that Majorana 1 chip will enable quantum computing.
II. Majorana 1 chip has been introduced by Amazon Web Services (AWS).
III. Deep learning is a subset of machine learning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Microsoft, not AWS, unveiled the Majorana 1 quantum chip. Deep learning is a subset of machine learning.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q47

questions.q:
With reference to monoclonal antibodies, often mentioned in news, consider the following statements:
I. They are man-made proteins.
II. They stimulate immunological function due to their ability to bind to specific antigens.
III. They are used in treating viral infections like that of Nipah virus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Monoclonal antibodies are lab-made proteins that bind specific antigens, and one was used against Nipah virus in India. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q48

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. No virus can survive in ocean waters.
II. No virus can infect bacteria.
III. No virus can change the cellular transcriptional activity in host cells.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Viruses are abundant in seawater, bacteriophages infect bacteria, and many viruses alter host gene activity. None of the statements holds.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q49

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Activated carbon is a good and an attractive tool to remove pollutants from effluent streams and to remediate contaminants from various industries.
Statement II: Activated carbon exhibits a large surface area and a strong potential for adsorbing heavy metals.
Statement III: Activated carbon can be easily synthesized from environmental wastes with high carbon content.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: Activated carbon's large surface area adsorbs heavy metals, and it can be made cheaply from carbon-rich waste. Both explain its value in treating effluents.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q50

questions.q:
With reference to the Indian polity, consider the following statements:
I. An Ordinance can amend any Central Act.
II. An Ordinance can abridge a Fundamental Right.
III. An Ordinance can come into effect from a back date.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: An ordinance has the force of law, so it can amend Central Acts and can apply retrospectively. It cannot abridge Fundamental Rights, as Article 13 covers ordinances.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q51

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: State Description
I. Arunachal Pradesh The capital is named after a fort, and the State has two National Parks
II. Nagaland The State came into existence on the basis of a Constitutional Amendment Act
III. Tripura Initially a Part ‘C’ State, it became a centrally administered territory with the reorganization of States in 1956 and later attained the status of a full-fledged State
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Itanagar is named after the Ita fort and Arunachal has two national parks; Nagaland was created by the 13th Amendment; Tripura went from Part C State to UT (1956) to full state (1972). All three match.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q52

questions.q:
With reference to India, consider the following:
I. The Inter-State Council
II. The National Security Council
III. Zonal Councils
How many of the above were established as per the provisions of the Constitution of India?
questions.e: Only the Inter-State Council is constitutional (Article 263). Zonal Councils are statutory and the NSC executive.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q53

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Constitution of India explicitly mentions that in certain spheres the Governor of a State acts in his/her own discretion.
II. The President of India can, of his/her own, reserve a bill passed by a State Legislature for his/her consideration without it being forwarded by the Governor of the State concerned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Constitution expressly allows the Governor discretion in some matters (Article 163). The President cannot reserve a State bill on her own; only the Governor can reserve it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q54

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Provision in the Constitution of India Stated under
I. Separation of Judiciary from the Executive in the public services of the State The Directive Principles of the State Policy
II. Valuing and preserving of the rich heritage of our composite culture The Fundamental Duties
III. Prohibition of employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories The Fundamental Rights
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Separation of judiciary (Art 50) is a DPSP, preserving composite culture (Art 51A(f)) a Fundamental Duty, and the ban on child labour in factories (Art 24) a Fundamental Right. All three match.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q55

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: With reference to the Constitution of India, if an area in a State is declared as Scheduled Area under the Fifth Schedule
I. the State Government loses its executive power in such areas and a local body assumes total administration
II. the Union Government can take over the total administration of such areas under certain circumstances on the recommendations of the Governor
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Scheduled Areas stay under State administration; the Union can only give directions. Neither statement is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q56

questions.q:
With reference to India, consider the following pairs: Organization Union Ministry
I. The National Automotive Board Ministry of Commerce and Industry
II. The Coir Board Ministry of Heavy Industries
III. The National Centre for Trade Information Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: The National Automotive Board is under Heavy Industries, the Coir Board under MSME, and the National Centre for Trade Information under Commerce. None matches.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q57

questions.q:
Consider the following subjects under the Constitution of India:
I. List I–Union List, in the Seventh Schedule
II. Extent of the executive power of a State
III. Conditions of the Governor's office For a constitutional amendment with respect to which of the above, ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States is required before presenting the bill to the President of India for assent?
questions.e: Amendments to the Seventh Schedule lists and the extent of State executive power need ratification by half the States. The Governor's conditions of office do not.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q58

questions.q:
With reference to the Indian polity, consider the following statements:
I. The Governor of a State is not answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his/her office.
II. No criminal proceedings shall be instituted or continued against the Governor during his/her term of office.
III. Members of a State Legislature are not liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said within the House.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 361 protects the Governor from court for official acts and from criminal proceedings during the term, and Article 194 protects legislators' speech in the House. All three.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q59

questions.q:
Consider the following activities:
I. Production of crude oil
II. Refining, storage and distribution of petroleum
III. Marketing and sale of petroleum products
IV. Production of natural gas
How many of the above activities are regulated by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board in our country?
questions.e: PNGRB regulates refining, storage, distribution, marketing and sale of petroleum and gas. Production of crude oil and natural gas is excluded.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q60

questions.q:
Suppose the revenue expenditure is ₹ 80,000 crores and the revenue receipts of the Government are ₹ 60,000 crores. The Government budget also shows borrowings of ₹ 10,000 crores and interest payments of ₹ 6,000 crores. Which of the following statements are correct?
I. Revenue deficit is ₹ 20,000 crores.
II. Fiscal deficit is ₹ 10,000 crores.
III. Primary deficit is ₹ 4,000 crores.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Revenue deficit = 80,000 − 60,000 = 20,000; fiscal deficit = borrowings = 10,000; primary deficit = 10,000 − 6,000 = 4,000. All three correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q61

questions.q: India is one of the founding members of the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC), a multimodal transportation corridor, which will connect
o: India to Central Asia to Europe via Iran
India to Central Asia via China
India to South-East Asia through Bangladesh and Myanmar
questions.e: INSTC links India to Central Asia, Russia and Europe through Iran.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q62

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Of the two major ethanol producers in the world, i.e., Brazil and the United States of America, the former produces more ethanol than the latter.
Statement-II: Unlike in the United States of America where corn is the principal feedstock for ethanol production, sugarcane is the principal feedstock for ethanol production in Brazil.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
questions.e: The USA, not Brazil, is the largest ethanol producer. US ethanol comes mainly from corn and Brazil's from sugarcane.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q63

questions.q:
The World Bank warned that India could become one of the first places where wet-bulb temperatures routinely exceed 35 °C. Which of the following statements best reflect(s) the implication of the above-said report?
I. Peninsular India will most likely suffer from flooding, tropical cyclones and droughts.
II. The survival of animals including humans will be affected as shedding of their body heat through perspiration becomes difficult.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Wet-bulb temperatures above 35°C make cooling by sweating impossible, threatening survival. UPSC's key also accepts higher risks of floods, cyclones and droughts in peninsular India.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q64

questions.q: A country's fiscal deficit stands at ₹ 50,000 crores. It is receiving ₹ 10,000 crores through non-debt creating capital receipts. The country's interest liabilities are ₹ 1,500 crores. What is the gross primary deficit?
questions.e: Gross primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest = 50,000 − 1,500 = ₹48,500 crore.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q65

questions.q:
Which of the following statements with regard to recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission of India are correct?
I. It has recommended grants of ₹ 4,800 crores from the year 2022–23 to the year 2025–26 for incentivizing States to enhance educational outcomes.
II. 45% of the net proceeds of Union taxes are to be shared with States.
III. ₹ 45,000 crores are to be kept as performance-based incentive for all States for carrying out agricultural reforms.
IV. It reintroduced tax effort criteria to reward fiscal performance.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The 15th FC recommended ₹4,800 crore for education outcomes, ₹45,000 crore for agricultural reforms, and reintroduced tax effort. The States' share was 41%, not 45%.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q66

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD):
I. It provides loans and guarantees to middle income countries.
II. It works single-handedly to help developing countries to reduce poverty.
III. It was established to help Europe rebuild after the World War II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The IBRD lends to middle-income countries and was set up to rebuild post-war Europe. It works alongside IDA and others, not alone.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q67

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of RTGS and NEFT:
I. In RTGS, the settlement time is instantaneous while in case of NEFT, it takes some time to settle payments.
II. In RTGS, the customer is charged for inward transactions while that is not the case for NEFT.
III. Operating hours for RTGS are restricted on certain days while this is not true for NEFT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: RTGS settles each transaction instantly, NEFT in half-hourly batches. Inward RTGS is free, and both run 24x7.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q68

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
I. United Arab Emirates
II. France
III. Germany
IV. Singapore
V. Bangladesh
How many countries amongst the above are there other than India where international merchant payments are accepted under UPI?
questions.e: UPI merchant payments work in the UAE, France and Singapore. Germany and Bangladesh were not on the list.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q69

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana':
I. It targets installation of one crore solar rooftop panels in the residential sector.
II. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy aims to impart training on installation, operation, maintenance and repairs of solar rooftop systems at grassroot levels.
III. It aims to create more than three lakhs skilled manpower through fresh skilling, and up-skilling, under scheme component of capacity building.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PM Surya Ghar targets one crore rooftop solar homes, with grassroots training and over three lakh skilled workers. All three.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q70

questions.q: "Sedition has become my religion" was the famous statement given by Gandhiji at the time of
o: publicly violating Salt Law at Dandi
attending the Second Round Table Conference in London
the launch of the Quit India Movement
questions.e: Gandhi said 'sedition has become my religion' during the Salt March of 1930.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q71

questions.q: The famous female figurine known as 'Dancing Girl', found at Mohenjo-daro, is made of
questions.e: The Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-daro is a bronze figure made by the lost-wax method.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q72

questions.q: Who provided legal defence to the people arrested in the aftermath of Chauri Chaura incident?
o: Madan Mohan Malaviya and Krishna Kant
Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Khwaja Hasan Nizami
questions.e: Madan Mohan Malaviya defended the Chauri Chaura accused; UPSC's option pairs him with Krishna Kant.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q73

questions.q: Subsequent to which one of the following events, Gandhiji, who consistently opposed untouchability and appealed for its eradication from all spheres, decided to include the upliftment of 'Harijans' in his political and social programme?
o: Arrest of Congress leadership at the time of the Quit India Movement
Promulgation of the Government of India Act, 1935
questions.e: After the Poona Pact (1932) Gandhi made Harijan upliftment part of his programme, founding the Harijan Sevak Sangh and the weekly Harijan.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q74

questions.q:
Consider the following fruits:
I. Papaya
II. Pineapple
III. Guava
How many of the above were introduced in India by the Portuguese in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries?
questions.e: Papaya, pineapple and guava are New World fruits brought to India through the Portuguese.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q75

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
I. United Kingdom
II. Denmark
III. New Zealand
IV. Australia
V. Brazil
How many of the above countries have more than four time zones?
questions.e: Counting overseas territories, the UK, Denmark (with Greenland), New Zealand and Australia have more than four time zones. Brazil has four.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q76

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Anadyr in Siberia and Nome in Alaska are a few kilometers from each other, but when people are waking up and getting set for breakfast in these cities, it would be different days.
II. When it is Monday in Anadyr, it is Tuesday in Nome.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Anadyr and Nome lie on opposite sides of the International Date Line, so they are on different days. Monday in Anadyr is Sunday in Nome.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q77

questions.q: Who among the following was the founder of the 'Self-Respect Movement'?
questions.e: E.V. Ramasamy 'Periyar' founded the Self-Respect Movement in 1925.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q78

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Country Resource-rich in
I. Botswana Diamond
II. Chile Lithium
III. Indonesia Nickel In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Botswana is rich in diamonds, Chile in lithium and Indonesia in nickel. All three match.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q79

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Region Country
I. Mallorca Italy
II. Normandy Spain
III. Sardinia France In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Mallorca is Spanish, Normandy French and Sardinia Italian. None matches.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q80

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Some rare earth elements are used in the manufacture of flat television screens and computer monitors.
Statement-II: Some rare earth elements have phosphorescent properties.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Rare earth compounds like europium and yttrium are used as phosphors that give colour in screens. II explains I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q81

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Indian Railways have prepared a National Rail Plan (NRP) to create a 'future ready' railway system by 2028.
II. 'Kavach' is an Automatic Train Protection system developed in collaboration with Germany.
III. 'Kavach' system consists of RFID tags fitted on track in station section.
Which of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.e: The National Rail Plan targets 2030, not 2028, and Kavach is indigenous, not developed with Germany. Kavach does use RFID tags on the track.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q82

questions.q:
Consider the following space missions:
I. Axiom-4
II. SpaDeX
III. Gaganyaan
How many of the space missions given above encourage and support micro-gravity research?
questions.e: Axiom-4 and Gaganyaan support microgravity research. UPSC's key does not count SpaDeX, a docking demonstration.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q83

questions.q:
With reference to India's defence, consider the following pairs: Aircraft type Description
I. Dornier-228 Maritime patrol aircraft
II. IL-76 Supersonic combat aircraft
III.
C-17 Globemaster III Military transport aircraft
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Dornier-228 is a maritime patrol aircraft and the C-17 a military transport. The IL-76 is a heavy-lift transport, not a combat jet.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q84

questions.q: Artificial way of causing rainfall to reduce air pollution makes use of
questions.e: Cloud seeding for artificial rain uses silver iodide, often with potassium iodide.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q85

questions.q:
Consider the following statements with regard to pardoning power of the President of India:
I. The exercise of this power by the President can be subjected to limited judicial review.
II. The President can exercise this power without the advice of the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The President's pardoning power is open to limited judicial review, but it must be exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. On the dissolution of the House of the People, the Speaker shall not vacate his/her office until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People after the dissolution.
II. According to the provisions of the Constitution of India, a Member of the House of the People on being elected as Speaker shall resign from his/her political party immediately.
III. The Speaker of the House of the People may be removed from his/her office by a resolution of the House of the People passed by a majority of all the then Members of the House, provided that no resolution shall be moved unless at least fourteen days' notice has been given of the intention to move the resolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Speaker continues after dissolution until the new House meets, and can be removed by a majority of all members after 14 days' notice. The Constitution does not require resigning from the party.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. If any question arises as to whether a Member of the House of the People has become subject to disqualification under the 10th Schedule, the President's decision in accordance with the opinion of the Council of Union Ministers shall be final.
II. There is no mention of the word 'political party' in the Constitution of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Tenth Schedule disqualification is decided by the Speaker or Chairman, not the President. The term 'political party' does appear in the Constitution (Tenth Schedule).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q88

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In India, State Governments have no power for making rules for grant of concessions in respect of extraction of minor minerals even though such minerals are located in their territories.
Statement-II: In India, the Central Government has the power to notify minor minerals under the relevant law.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
questions.e: States make the rules for minor mineral concessions, so Statement I is wrong. The Centre notifies which minerals are minor.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q89

questions.q: Which organization has enacted the Nature Restoration Law (NRL) to tackle climate change and biodiversity loss?
o: The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development
questions.e: The European Union adopted the Nature Restoration Law in 2024.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Panchayats at the intermediate level exist in all States.
II. To be eligible to be a Member of a Panchayat at the intermediate level, a person should attain the age of thirty years.
III. The Chief Minister of a State constitutes a commission to review the financial position of Panchayats at the intermediate levels and to make recommendations regarding the distribution of net proceeds of taxes and duties, leviable by the State, between the State and Panchayats at the intermediate level.
Which of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.e: States under 20 lakh population need not have intermediate panchayats, the minimum age is 21, and the State Finance Commission is set up by the Governor. All three are incorrect.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of BIMSTEC:
I. It is a regional organization consisting of seven member States till January 2025.
II. It came into existence with the signing of the Dhaka Declaration, 1999.
III. Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Thailand and Nepal are founding member States of BIMSTEC.
IV. In BIMSTEC, the subsector of 'tourism' is being led by India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: BIMSTEC has seven members. It began with the Bangkok Declaration (1997); Nepal joined later; and tourism is led by Nepal. Only I is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q92

questions.q:
Who amongst the following are members of the Jury to select the recipient of 'Gandhi Peace Prize'?
I. The President of India
II. The Prime Minister of India
III. The Chief Justice of India
IV. The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Gandhi Peace Prize jury is chaired by the Prime Minister and includes the CJI and the Leader of Opposition, not the President.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q93

questions.q:
GPS-Aided Geo Augmented Navigation (GAGAN) uses a system of ground stations to provide necessary augmentation. Which of the following statements is/are correct in respect of GAGAN?
I. It is designed to provide additional accuracy and integrity.
II. It will allow more uniform and high quality air traffic management.
III. It will provide benefits only in aviation but not in other modes of transportation.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: GAGAN improves GPS accuracy and integrity and supports air traffic management. It also benefits other transport sectors, so III is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q94

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding AI Action Summit held in Grand Palais, Paris in February 2025:
I. Co-chaired with India, the event builds on the advances made at the Bletchley Park Summit held in 2023 and the Seoul Summit held in 2024.
II. Along with other countries, US and UK also signed the declaration on inclusive and sustainable AI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Paris AI Action Summit, co-chaired by India, followed Bletchley Park and Seoul. The US and UK did not sign the declaration.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q95

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
I. International Year of the Woman Farmer: 2026
II. International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism: 2027
III. International Year of Peace and Trust: 2025
IV. International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence: 2029
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The UN has declared 2025 Peace and Trust, 2026 Woman Farmer, 2027 Sustainable Tourism and 2029 Asteroid Awareness. All four match.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q96

questions.q:
Consider the following statements with regard to BRICS:
I. 16th BRICS Summit was held under the Chairship of Russia in Kazan.
II. Indonesia has become a full member of BRICS.
III. The theme of the 16th BRICS Summit was Strengthening Multiculturalism for Just Global Development and Security.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 16th BRICS Summit was in Kazan under Russia and Indonesia joined as a full member. The theme was 'Strengthening Multilateralism', not 'Multiculturalism'.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q97

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Lokpal:
I. The power of Lokpal applies to public servants of India, but not to the Indian public servants posted outside India.
II. The Chairperson or a Member shall not be a Member of the Parliament or a Member of the Legislature of any State or Union Territory, and only the Chief Justice of India, whether incumbent or retired, has to be its Chairperson.
III. The Chairperson or a Member shall not be a person of less than forty-five years of age on the date of assuming office as the Chairperson or Member, as the case may be.
IV. Lokpal cannot inquire into the allegations of corruption against a sitting Prime Minister of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
o: None of the above statements is correct
questions.e: Lokpal members must be at least 45. The Lokpal covers public servants abroad too, may be chaired by a judge or eminent person, and can inquire into the PM with safeguards.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q98

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the first Kho Kho World Cup:
I. The event was held in Delhi, India.
II. Indian men beat Nepal with a score of 78–40 in the final to become the World Champion in men category.
III. Indian women beat Nepal with a score of 54–36 in the final to become the World Champion in women category.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The first Kho Kho World Cup was in New Delhi and India won both titles. The scores in II and III are swapped.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q99

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. In the finals of the 45th Chess Olympiad held in 2024, Gukesh Dommaraju became the world's youngest winner after defeating the Russian player Ian Nepomniachtchi.
II. Abhimanyu Mishra, an American chess player, holds the record of becoming world's youngest ever Grandmaster.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Gukesh became the youngest world champion by beating Ding Liren, not in the Olympiad. Abhimanyu Mishra of the USA is the youngest-ever Grandmaster.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, GS Paper I, Q100
